items.text: London’s Hamleys toy store is predicting Christmas toy hits for this year with many types of toys. Fuggler is a doll with a strange head and life-like teeth; kids like its imperfection theme . Gravitrax is a building toy that teaches about track systems. Monopoly has a version of its board game for cheaters . The popular toys run from £8 to £80 and some British adults spend over £150 on their children at Christmas to get the right toys. Difficult words: theme (a general idea about something), cheater (a person who cheats – does not play fair). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A London toy store is predicting popular Christmas toys for this year with many types of toys. Fuggler is a doll with an unusual head and teeth; kids like its imperfection theme . Gravitrax is a building toy that teaches about building tracks. Monopoly has a version of its board game for cheaters . These toys are from £8 to £80 and some British parents spend over £150 on their children at Christmas. Difficult words: predict (to try to tell what will happen), imperfection (when something is not perfect), theme (the main idea about something), cheater (a person who cheats – does not play fair). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is a toy store in London. It is predicting Christmas toy hits for this year. There are many types of toys. Fuggler is a doll with an unusual head and teeth. Gravitrax is a track-building toy. Monopoly has a type of its board game for cheaters . These toys are from £8 to £80. Some British adults spend over £150 on Christmas toys. Difficult words: predict (try to tell what can happen), cheater (a person who cheats – does not play fair). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Nobel Committee is going to decide this year’s winner of the Nobel Peace Prize, and Donald Trump may get a nomination. If Trump wins, he would be one of many controversial people who won the award. In 1973, Henry Kissinger won the award for his North Vietnam peace talks, despite that critics said that he was part of America’s secret bombing raids in Cambodia and in Vietnam. In 1991, Aung San Suu Kyi won the award as she fought to help Myanmar become democratic. Critics now denounce her as a leader for her inaction to stop ethnic cleansing happening there. In 1994, Yasser Arafat won the award for trying to bring peace to Palestine and to Israel in the Oslo Accords. Many critics said that he was behind terrorism that killed Israeli civilians . In 2009, Barack Obama won an award for trying to help the people of the world cooperate. Critics say that he did not help because of involvement in the Libyan war. Difficult words: controversial (arguable, debatable), raid (a sudden attack), denounce (criticise), intervene (step in), civilian (a person who is not part of the military). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Trump may get a nomination for the Nobel Peace Prize. If he wins, he would be one of many controversial people who won the award. Henry Kissinger won the award for his North Vietnam peace talks, but critics say that he was part of America’s secret bombing raids in Cambodia and in Vietnam. Aung San Suu Kyi won the award as she fought to help Myanmar become democratic, but critics say that she is not stopping the ethnic cleansing happening there now. Yasser Arafat won the award for trying to bring peace to Palestine and to Israel, but critics say that he was part of terrorism against Israel. Barack Obama won an award for trying to help the people of the world work together, but critics say that he was also involved in the Libyan war. Difficult words: controversial (you can argue against something if it is controversial), raid (a quick attack), ethnic cleansing (when a people tries to kill off or send away another group of people who are different than them). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Trump may get the Nobel Peace Prize. It will be controversial if he wins. He will not be alone. Henry Kissinger wins when he has talks to help North Vietnam. Critics say that he bombs Vietnam and Cambodia. Aung San Suu Kyi wins the prize, too. She makes the government of Myanmar democratic. Now, critics say that she is not stopping attacks against people there. Yasser Arafat wins when he tries to help with peace in Israel and Palestine. Critics say that he attacks Israel. Barack Obama wins when he tries to help the people of the world. Critics say that he was also part of the Libyan war. Difficult words: controversial (people think different things about controversial problems), will (in the future), government (the bosses of a country), was (past of ‘is’). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

At an event near Cadiz in Spain, the company Hyperloop Transportation Technologies (HTT) unveiled its first full-scale passenger capsule . The company has signed deals with the United Arab Emirates, China and Ukraine and hopes to run services in Spain. The co-founder and CEO of HTT said that a hyperloop between Madrid and Barcelona would cut the journey to 20–25 minutes. The ‘Hyperloop’ is a new mode of transportation that Elon Musk first proposed in 2012. It has a potential of reaching speeds of up to 1,220 kilometres per hour. The capsule is now going to Toulouse in southern France for further assembly and testing. Difficult words: unveil (to show people something new for the first time), capsule (a special type of carriage), CEO (the chief executive officer, the boss), assembly (putting something together, making it). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Spain, people unveiled the first full-scale passenger capsule . The company which made the capsule is called the Hyperloop Transportation Technologies (HTT). HTT already has deals with the United Arab Emirates, China and Ukraine and it hopes to run services in Spain. The CEO of HTT said that a hyperloop between Madrid and Barcelona would cut the journey to 20–25 minutes. The ‘Hyperloop’ is a new mode of transportation. Elon Musk first proposed it in 2012. It can go as fast as 1,220 kilometres per hour. The capsule will now go to Toulouse in southern France for testing. Difficult words: capsule (a special type of carriage), unveil (to show people something new for the first time), CEO (the chief executive officer, the boss). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The ‘Hyperloop’ is a new type of transportation. It can go up to 1,220 kilometres per hour. People are working to make the Hyperloop a reality. A company called Hyperloop Transportation Technologies makes a hyperloop capsule . It is full scale in size . They show it to people for the first time in Spain. If a hyperloop is built between Madrid and Barcelona, you can make the trip in 20–25 minutes. Difficult words: capsule (a special type of carriage), full scale (the actual size), size (how big something is). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The painting ‘Girl With Balloon’ by the elusive artist Banksy self-destructed moments after being sold for £1.04m at auction. There was a shredder embedded in the frame of the painting which turned on after the piece went under the hammer at Sotheby’s auction in London. People at the auction were shocked. Some thought that the shredding was not real, and that it was all a stunt , but everything was real. The painting, the price and its destruction were all real. People approached by the media thought that it was original and ingenious – a turning point for art. Difficult words: elusive (difficult to identify), shredder (a machine for cutting something into pieces), embedded (built-in), go under the hammer (be sold at an auction), stunt (something unusual to attract attention), approached (asked what they think on camera), ingenious (imaginative and creative). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People at the auction of Banksy’s ‘Girl With Balloon’ were in for a shock because after the painting was sold for £1.04m, it self-destructed. It turned out that there was a shredder embedded in the frame of the painting. It turned on after the painting was sold, and people thought that it was a joke but the whole thing was real – the painting, the price, and its destruction. Some people said that the shredding was original and ingenious . Difficult words: self-destruct (destroy itself), shredder (a machine for cutting something into pieces), embedded (built-in), ingenious (very imaginative). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A Banksy painting went on auction in London. The name of the painting is ‘Girl With Balloon’. It sells for £1.04m. However, things do not go as people expect . There is a shredder inside the frame of the painting. It turns on after the painting is sold. People are shocked. Everything is real. It is not a joke. Some people think that it is original and very clever. Difficult words: expect (when you expect something, you think that it is going to happen), shredder (a machine for cutting something into pieces), frame (the wood around the picture). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last Wednesday, a school bus carrying 42 students crashed in a suburb in Dallas . One child died and three children, the driver and three officers were injured. The police said that the bus struck a power line and ignited a fire but the exact cause of the crash is still being investigated. Difficult words: suburb (an outlying area of a city), Dallas (a big city in Texas, USA), ignite (start suddenly). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last Wednesday in Texas, USA, a school bus carrying 42 students crashed and killed one child. Three children, the driver, and three officers were injured. The bus hit a power line and created a fire. However, the cause of the crash is being investigated . Difficult words: cause (the reason – why something happened), investigate (collect information and understand why something happened). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Dallas is in Texas. Texas is in the USA. A school bus crashes there. The bus is carrying 42 students. One child dies. Three children are injured. The driver and three officers are injured, too. People are investigating the crash. Difficult words: crash (hit something), officer (someone like a policeman/policewoman or a security guard), investigate (get more information about and understand why something happened). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Mexican volcano Popocatepetl recently erupted, spewing ash and smoke into the air. The first activity started on 21st September in the evening. The ash fell in a nearby town and, along with the smoke, people could see it for miles. The government warned local residents to stay away from the area. A massive earthquake in February triggered the volcano’s prior eruption. Difficult words: spew (send out with a lot of force), prior (earlier, the one before), trigger (start). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Popocatepetl is a volcano in Mexico that erupted in February because of a powerful earthquake. Recently, the volcano erupted again, and it spewed ash and smoke into the air which you could see for miles. Its activity started 21st September in the evening. Ash fell in a nearby town, and the government warned local residents to stay away from the dangerous area. Difficult words: spew (send out with a lot of force), ash (a very soft grey material which is produced when something burns), resident (a person who resides – lives somewhere). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Popocatepetl is a volcano in Mexico. It erupts in February. It erupts because of an earthquake . Popocatepetl erupts this September again. You can see the smoke for miles. Ash falls on a nearby town. Difficult words: erupt (be active and dangerous, send out smoke and hot things), earthquake (when the ground moves), ash (very soft grey things that come out of burned up stuff). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An adorable baby orangutan named Lily has been born via C-section at a zoo in Kansas, USA, to 33-year-old mother Daisy. Lily, the youngest of the mother’s three offspring , is doing well and slowly is beginning to spend more time with her family and away from vets. The mother Daisy is doing well, too. Difficult words: adorable (lovable, sweet, cute, beautiful), C-section (also a caesarean section – when the baby is born through space which is cut in the mother belly), offspring singular = plural (an animal’s child). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

An adorable baby orangutan named Lily was born at a zoo in Kansas, USA. Lily’s mother Daisy is 33 years old, and Lily is her third and youngest baby. Lily was born via C-section and both the mother and the daughter are OK. Lily is beginning to spend more time with her orangutan family and away from vets. Difficult words: adorable (lovable, sweet, cute, beautiful), via (through), C-section (also a caesarean section – when doctors help the mother give birth by operating on her to the baby out), both (the two of them). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A baby orangutan is born in a zoo in Kansas, USA. Her name is Lily. She is very cute . She is born from a C-section . Her mother is 33 years old. Her name is Daisy. Lily is Daisy’s third and youngest baby. Both the mother and the daughter are fine. Difficult words: cute (sweet and beautiful – like a baby), C-section (also a caesarean section – when doctors cut the baby out of the mother’s belly to help the mother give birth), both (the two of them). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Two thousand marine animals swim from the ocean into the River Thames in England every year, and there are many types of animals. In 2016, a seal climbed onto the beach near the London Eye . In 2017, people spotted a porpoise near Richmond. Most recently, people saw a Beluga whale near Kent. They named him Benny and said that he is lost as he should be in cooler Arctic waters. Difficult words: London Eye (a giant Ferris wheel sitting above the River Thames), porpoise (a small-toothed whale similar to the dolphin). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Two thousand marine animals swim into the River Thames in England every year. In 2016, a seal came onto a beach, and in 2017, people saw a porpoise . This year, people saw a Beluga whale . They named him Benny and said that he is lost because he should be in cooler waters. Difficult words: marine (from the ocean), porpoise (a small whale similar to the dolphin), Beluga whale (a white whale that lives in water around the Arctic). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The River Thames is a big river in England. It flows through London. It goes out to the ocean. Two thousand marine animals swim into the river every year. In 2016, people see a seal. In 2017, people see a porpoise . This year, people see a Beluga whale . They name him Benny. They say that he is lost. Beluga whales usually live in cold water. Difficult words: marine (ocean), porpoise (a small whale like the dolphin), Beluga whale (a white whale that lives in very cold water). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Almost one year has passed since an illegal referendum for Catalonian independence took place. In San Jaume Square, Barcelona, protesters for Catalan faced off against riot police, who began fighting the protesters after the protesters hurled paint and projectiles . Police were trying to keep the protesters away from another protest group who wants the police to get better pay. Police arrested one man as this protest turned into violence. Spain’s government is in a financial crisis , and political tensions are high in Catalonia. Difficult words: referendum (when people vote yes or no for something), hurl (throw with a lot of force), projectile (something that people throw as a weapon), crisis (a problematic situation), political tensions (problems, bad relations between people in politics). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Catalonian independence referendum in Spain took place almost one year ago. In a square in Barcelona, pro-Catalan protesters fought against riot police after the protesters threw paint and objects. Police were trying to keep the protesters away from other protesters who want the police to get better pay. Police arrested one man as the protest turned violent. Spain’s government has serious money problems, and political tensions are high in Catalonia. Difficult words: independence referendum (when people vote yes or no for a big change, such as Catalonia to become a new country), riot police (police who try to control large groups of people who might riot – cause violence), political tension (problems, bad relations between people in politics). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This happens a year ago. Catalonia is an area in Barcelona, Spain. The people there want Catalonia to break off from Spain. They want it to be a new country. There is a referendum . Spain says that this referendum is illegal . Spain does not like Catalonia be a new country. Now protesters fight against riot police . The police want to keep them away from other protesters. People get violent . Spain’s government has serious money problems. The government leaders are worried. The people in Catalonia are very worried. Difficult words: referendum (when people vote yes or no for something in the country to change, like Catalonia becoming a new country), illegal (against the law), riot police (police who try to control large groups of people who can be violent), violent (when you are violent, you can break things or hurt people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Police in the Netherlands say that they have foiled an attempt to commit a major terrorist attack when they arrested seven suspects aged between 21 and 34. Intelligence services say that the ringleader wanted to hit a large event ‘with lots of victims’, planning to use assault rifles , grenades and a car bomb. Difficult words: foil (prevent, stop from happening), attempt (trying to do something), suspect (a person who is thought to be guilty of a crime), ringleader (a person who leads an illegal activity), assault rifle (a type of big gun). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Police in the Netherlands say that they prevented a major terrorist attack when they arrested seven suspects aged between 21 and 34. They say that the terrorists wanted to hit an event of a lot of people. Difficult words: prevent (stop from happening), major (big), suspect (a person who police think is a criminal). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Police in the Netherlands arrest seven people. They suspect that they are terrorists. The suspects are aged between 21 and 34. The police say that they stop a big terrorist attack by arresting them. Difficult words: suspect verb (think), suspect noun (a person who police think is a criminal). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Air Niugini’s Boeing 737 (a Papua New Guinean airline) was trying to land on Chuuk Island in the Federated States of Micronesia, but it was forced to crash-land in a Pacific lagoon. All of the crew and 40–50 passengers on-board survived. One of the crash survivors said that, unfortunately, the flight attendants panicked and started yelling. On the other hand, the locals really impressed him with their help, when they immediately started coming out on boats to help them. He escaped only with a grazed forehead, but he said that some people were injured severely. Difficult words: impressed (feel respect for, admire), grazed (scratched). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A Boeing 737 was trying to land on Chuuk Island in the Federated States of Micronesia when it had to crash-land in a Pacific lagoon. All of the crew and 40–50 passengers on-board survived. One survivor said that the flight attendants panicked and started yelling. On the other hand, the help of the locals impressed him, as they immediately started coming out on boats to help them. He escaped with only a grazed forehead, but he said that some people were injured severely . Difficult words: impressed (feel respect for, admire), grazed (scratched), severely (badly). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Chuuk Island is in Micronesia. A plane wants to land on the island. It is a Boeing 737. The plane does not land at an airport. It crash-lands in the lagoon . There are 40–50 passengers on board. All of them survive . All of the crew survives, too. Difficult words: lagoon (a lake that is seawater and is separate from the ocean), survive (to live after something bad happens), crew (the people who work on an aeroplane). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A 7.5-magnitude earthquake hit near the Indonesian island of Sulawesi, triggering a 3-metre tsunami, which smashed into two cities on the coast. Palu and Donggala are the cities affected the worst, and they are home to over 600,000 people. At least 832 people have been confirmed dead, thousands of homes collapsed, along with hospitals, hotels, and a shopping centre. The disaster affected as many as 1.6 million people, according to Red Cross estimates . Difficult words: trigger (start), estimate (a careful guess based on data). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A 7.5- magnitude earthquake hit near the Indonesian island of Sulawesi which triggered a 3-metre tsunami that smashed into two cities on the coast. These cities are home to 600,000 people. The tsunami killed more than 832 people and destroyed hospitals, hotels, a shopping centre, and thousands of homes. The event affected the lives of as many as 1.6 million people. Difficult words: magnitude (the size of power of something), trigger (start suddenly), smash (move into with a lot of force). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Sulawesi is an island in Indonesia. An earthquake hits near it. The earthquake makes a tsunami . It is 3 metres tall. The tsunami moves into two cities. Around 600,000 people live there. More than 832 people die. Hospitals, hotels, a shopping centre, and thousands of homes are destroyed . Difficult words: earthquake (when the ground moves), tsunami (a big wave started by an earthquake), destroy (break completely). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Thousands of spiders made a nearly 300-metre web stretching across a beach near a lagoon in western Greece. A biology professor said that the spiders are basically having a mating party underneath the cloudy blanket before dying due to coming cooler weather. The tiny spiders do not pose any dangers to humans or plants in the area, but their rising numbers may be linked to an increase in mosquito populations. The webs are beautiful and creepy at the same time, as they cover trees and boats. Difficult words: stretch (exist over an area), mate (make babies), tiny (very small), creepy (scary). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In western Greece, thousands of spiders made a 300-metre web near a lagoon . The webs are beautiful and creepy at the same time, as they cover trees and boats. It is possible that there are so many spiders because there are more mosquitoes. The spiders are very small and are not dangerous to people or plants. A biology professor said that the spiders are mating under the cloudy web and will soon die because of incoming cooler weather. Difficult words: lagoon (a lake that is near other lakes), creepy (scary), mate (make babies), incoming (coming). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Thousands of spiders make a very large web. It is 300 metres long. It is in western Greece. There are so many spiders because there are more mosquitoes . The web is beautiful. It is also a little scary. It covers trees and boats. The spiders are mating under the web. However, cool weather is coming. It will kill the spiders. The spiders are small. They are not dangerous to people. Difficult words: mosquito (a flying insect which can bite you and suck your blood), mate (make baby spiders), will (in the future). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A couple from Russia discovered that old vinyl records can be used more than once by transforming them into clocks. Most of the orders come from music fans ordering clocks with an image of their favourite band, like The Beatles, for example. Pavel Polukhin, the owner of the Cube Company, said that vinyl records are something from the past, old and already forgotten, but by transforming them into clocks, they give them a second life. Difficult words: order (when you ask that somebody makes something for you for money). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A couple from Russia is turning old vinyl records into clocks. Most of the orders come from music fans who order a clock with an image of their favourite band. The owner of the company said that vinyl records are something from the past but by transforming them into clocks, they give them a second life. Difficult words: order (when you ask that somebody makes something for you for money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People do not use vinyl record anymore. However, they can still be useful . A couple from Russia makes clocks out of them. The clocks often show the customer ’s favourite band. The vinyl records have a second life as a clock. Difficult words: vinyl record (a flat black circle which plays music), useful (when something is useful, it makes people’s lives better), customer (a person who buys something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In British Columbia, Canada, firefighters were fighting a fire when a firenado sucked their hose 100 feet into the air and melted it. The blaze was one of many wildfires occurring at that time. A firenado or fire whirl happens if wind gusts , heat from fire, and hot ground temperatures mix together, creating an uplift of air that pulls in fire, ash, and debris . Difficult words: firenado (a tornado that forms from wind and fire), melt (make soft or turn to liquid – something like water), blaze (a large fire), whirl (a swirling movement of air), gust (a strong wind), uplift (a wind that pulls things upwards), debris (broken down and small pieces of things). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In British Columbia, Canada, firefighters were fighting a fire when a firenado picked up their hose. It lifted it 100 feet into the air and then melted it. The fire was one of many wildfires happening. A firenado or fire whirl happens when wind, heat from fire, and hot ground temperatures mix together. The mix creates air that moves upwards and pulls in fire, ash, and debris . Difficult words: firenado (a wind storm that forms from wind and fire), melt (make soft or turn to liquid – something like water), whirl (when air moves in circles very quickly, tornado), debris (small pieces of things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Canada, there are many wildfires. Firefighters are fighting one. A firenado picks up their hose. It pulls it 100 feet into the air. Then it melts the hose. A firenado comes from a mix of wind, heat, and hot ground temperatures . The mix creates air that moves up. The air pulls in fire and small things. Difficult words: firenado (a fire tornado), melt (make soft or turn to liquid – something like water), temperature (how hot or cold something is). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hong Kong opened a new high-speed train link to inland China which cut down the journey from Hong Kong to Shenzhen by 45 minutes. The new system cost 10 billion US dollars, took eight years to complete and will carry over 80,000 passengers daily. The new speedy mode of transport provoked protests outside the station over Beijing’s increasing influence in the Hong Kong region. Difficult words: influence (power). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Hong Kong opened a new high-speed train that connects Hong Kong to Shenzen and cuts the journey by 45 minutes. The new system cost 10 billion US dollars, took eight years to complete and will carry 80,000 passengers daily. The new system provoked protests outside the station, as some people are worried about Beijing’s increasing influence in the Hong Kong region. Difficult words: journey (a long trip), provoke (cause), increasing (getting bigger and bigger), influence (power). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hong Kong opens a new high-speed train. It connects Hong Kong to Shenzen. The new system cost 10 billion US dollars. It took eight years to build. It can carry 80,000 people a day. You can travel from Hong Kong to Shenzen in just 14 minutes. That is 45 minutes less than before. Hong Kong is not completely a part of China. Shenzen is in China. The new train brings Hong Kong and China more together. Some people do not like this. They protest. Difficult words: cost (past of ’cost’ – if something costs some money, you have to pay the money to have it), took (past of ‘take’). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Mangkhut is one of the most powerful typhoons to hit Southeast Asia in decades. It caused landslides in two villages in the northern Philippine mountain province of Benguet. Thirty-three people were confirmed dead and at least 29 people are still missing, according to local reports. Search and rescue missions continue among fears that the death toll could rise above 100. The typhoon continued west, bringing winds of up to 160 kilometres per hour to China’s most populous Guangdong province. Streets were completely flooded, people advised to stay inside, and nearly half a million people evacuated from cities. A scaffolding was blown off a building in Hong Kong by the strong winds. The typhoon is expected to weaken into a tropical depression (with winds below 62 kilometres per hour) as it moves inland. Difficult words: confirm (when people confirm something, they are sure that it is true), death toll (the number of dead people). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Mangkhut is a very powerful typhoon to hit Southeast Asia, as it caused landslides in two villages in the Philippines. Thirty-three people died and another 29 are still missing. People are looking for survivors , but they fear that up to 100 people died. The typhoon moved west to China. It brought strong winds to China’s Guangdong province. City streets were covered under water, and 500,000 people had to evacuate. A scaffolding was blown off a building in Hong Kong by the strong winds. The typhoon is moving inland and will become weaker. Difficult words: typhoon (a large tropical storm), survivor (somebody who survives – lives through something very hard), scaffolding (a structure on which builders stand to build or repair a building). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Mangkhut is a very powerful typhoon . It causes landslides in two villages in the Philippines. Thirty-three people die. Twenty-nine people are missing . The typhoon moves to China. It brings strong winds. City streets are under water. Around 500,000 people must evacuate . Then the typhoon moves west. It becomes weaker. Difficult words: typhoon (a big tropical storm), be missing (when you are missing, people do not know where you are and if you are OK), evacuate (move away because of danger). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A bus turned into a mobile church brings hop-on services to Christians living in remote villages in Russia’s Tatarstan Republic. For many worshippers, a journey to the nearest church is simply too far, and that is why Father Andrei Streblov created a mobile version. He said that he used to travel with a tent, but bad weather made that difficult. Additionally, the bus is decked out with icons , an altar and spires – just like a regular church. He travels once a week and the number of people there attending his services is increasing. Difficult words: remote (far from a town), decked out (decorated, coved in), icon (a painting of Christ or a saint), altar (the table in a Christian church that is the most important location of the church), spire (a little tower on a church). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Russia is a very big country and some people live in remote areas which can make things difficult; for some people a journey to the nearest church is simply too far. One priest in the Tatarstan Republic turned a bus into a mobile church. He travels once a week and more and more people attend his services. The bus is decorated with things that you would normally find in a church. Difficult words: remote (far from a town), journey (a long, difficult trip), attend (come to and be there). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Russia is a very big country. Some people live in remote areas. This can make things difficult. Some people cannot go to church. It is too far for them. One priest helps these people. He turns a bus into a mobile church. The bus has everything like a normal church. The priest travels once a week. More and more people come to his church. Difficult words: remote (far from a town), priest (a man of God who works in a church), mobile (something mobile can move). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

At least 29 people died and 70 others were wounded in an attack at a military parade in the Iranian city of Ahvaz this Saturday. The victims were both military personnel and civilians, including a journalist, who was watching the parade. People reported that security forces gunned down three of the attackers during clashes and arrested one. The separatist group the Patriotic Arab Democratic Movement claimed responsibility for the attack. It is an organisation which ‘foreign antagonists ’ support, including Saudi Arabia, as reported by the state-run Islamic Republic News Agency. Difficult words: wounded (injured), clash (a fight), antagonist (a rival or an enemy). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

This Saturday there was an attack at a military parade in Iran where at least 29 people died and 70 others were injured. The victims were both military personnel and civilians. People killed three of the attackers and arrested one. The separatist group the Patriotic Arab Democratic Movement claimed responsibility for the attack. Difficult words: military (the army), victim (a person who dies or is injured), separatist (a group which wants to separate – break off a piece of country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Texas, police attempted to arrest a woman due to warrants for her arrest, and she led them on a high-speed chase. Aerial footage caught the moment when she crashed into another car. After the crash, the woman rushed to get her baby who was in a car seat, and she ran across multiple roads. Police arrested the woman after she tried to car jack another vehicle, and they took her baby to Child Protective Services . Difficult words: warrant (an arrest warrant is an official document that a judge signed and says that the police can arrest someone), aerial (from the air), car jack (steal a car), Child Protective Services (an American government organisation that takes care of children and babies).
